criteria.absent: negligible or negative in every common state, own reference
criteria.across: positive: the household mean log ratio is at least log of the minimal ratio and its lower bound above 0; negative: at most minus that, upper bound below 0; negligible: the whole interval within plus or minus it; uncertain: anything else; insufficient: fewer than min_households households
criteria.cell: consistent: the observed log ratio lies within the central band of the replicates' log ratios; above or below: outside it, by at least the minimal ratio in that direction; small: outside it by less
criteria.partial: positive in one or two common states, own reference
criteria.roadmap: the roadmap names a next model family only if the routing indicates one
criteria.routing: a systematic excess of quiet runs or bursts points to within-state temporal dependence, which would also over-disperse the counts; otherwise systematic active dispersion points to an over-dispersed zero-truncated count model; otherwise no new family is indicated
criteria.systematic: positive in at least three of the four common states and negative in none, own reference

data.counts: each instrumented channel's activations in each 5-minute window, as the fitted channel models read them
data.external: the frozen external cohort is not touched
data.labels: truth_series of each recording's annotations; unlabelled windows are not used

distribution.rule: observed windows in each count bin against the reference's expected windows; the last bin is open

groups.room: each room, pooling a room's channels within a household
groups.state_channel: each state and channel: descriptive, no interval

households.use: the development panel only; each household is examined once, against its own hurdle fit and against the population fitted on its fold's training households

model.family: hurdle: silence with probability pi, otherwise a zero-truncated Poisson count with rate mu, per channel and state
model.inference: unchanged: no model is refitted for inference and no state is estimated

configuration.name: phase3-hurdle-predictive-checks

references.own: the hurdle fitted to the cell alone: pi its share of silent windows, mu solved from its active windows' mean; it reproduces the cell's silence, mean and active mean exactly, so those are not judged against it
references.population: the fold's population hurdle fitted on its training households with 12 pseudo-windows, as in the Phase 3.3 follow-up, applied unchanged

replicates.own: each replicate drawn from the cell's own fit and refitted before its statistics are computed: a parametric bootstrap
replicates.population: each replicate drawn from the population hurdle, not refitted: the predictive distribution for a new household
replicates.seed: numpy default_rng of (seed, household, state, channel, reference) indices

routes.dispersion: an over-dispersed zero-truncated count model for the active part, such as the zero-truncated negative binomial, keeping the hurdle's silence parameter
routes.temporal: within-state temporal dependence: activity sub-states or a Markov-modulated emission within each state; no marginal count family produces runs beyond independence given the state, and a latent intensity that varies over time also over-disperses the counts

runs.within: A maximal run of consecutive labelled windows of the cell's state; runs are counted within stretches.

statistics.active_dispersion: Variance of the active windows' counts over the zero-truncated Poisson's, m (1 + mu - m); a value above one means the model is under-dispersed.
statistics.active_mean: Mean count of the cell's active windows; the model's is mu / (1 - exp(-mu)).
statistics.bursts: Windows in maximal runs of at least burst_windows active windows within stretches, observed over the replicates' mean, with half a window added to each.
statistics.mean: Mean count over the cell's windows.
statistics.q90: The 90th percentile of the active windows' counts, the smallest count whose empirical share at or below it reaches 0.9, over the model's.
statistics.quiet_runs: Windows in maximal runs of at least quiet_run_windows silent windows within stretches, observed over the replicates' mean, with half a window added to each.
statistics.silence: Share of the cell's windows with no activation; compared as a log odds ratio with half a window added to each side.
statistics.tail_excess: Active windows above the model's 99th percentile, observed over expected, with half a window added to each.
statistics.variance: Variance of the count over the cell's windows, with one degree of freedom removed; the hurdle's is (1 - pi) (v + m^2) - ((1 - pi) m)^2 for the zero-truncated Poisson's mean m and variance v.

sufficiency.rule: a cell enters with at least min_windows labelled windows; active-window statistics need min_active active windows; a run statistic needs its observed or predicted windows in runs to reach min_runs times the run length; the own reference needs a silent and an active window

configuration.tuning: none: every threshold is declared; nothing is fitted on the statistics it is judged by
configuration.variance_mean: Least-squares slope of log active variance on log active mean across one household's cells with enough active windows: about 1 for Poisson-like counts, approaching 2 when the excess variance grows with the square of the mean.

evidence.reason: no state is estimated: the diagnostic compares observed channel counts in labelled windows with the observation model's predictive distribution

inference.label: online filter
inference.provenance: declared by the experiment that wrote the record

information_set.evidence: each instrumented channel's count in each labelled window
information_set.name: current

metric_definitions.active_mean: Mean count of the cell's active windows; the model's is mu / (1 - exp(-mu)).

metric_definitions.bursts: Windows in maximal runs of at least burst_windows active windows within stretches, observed over the replicates' mean, with half a window added to each.
metric_definitions.cell: One household's labelled windows of one state on one instrumented channel, in time order.
metric_definitions.household_value: For a group of cells, such as a state, the mean of one household's cell log ratios in the group.
metric_definitions.log_ratio: Log of the observed statistic over the reference's.
metric_definitions.mean: Mean count over the cell's windows.
metric_definitions.q90: The 90th percentile of the active windows' counts, the smallest count whose empirical share at or below it reaches 0.9, over the model's.
metric_definitions.quiet_runs: Windows in maximal runs of at least quiet_run_windows silent windows within stretches, observed over the replicates' mean, with half a window added to each.
metric_definitions.silence: Share of the cell's windows with no activation; compared as a log odds ratio with half a window added to each side.
metric_definitions.stretch: A maximal run of consecutive labelled windows of the cell's state; runs are counted within stretches.
metric_definitions.tail_excess: Active windows above the model's 99th percentile, observed over expected, with half a window added to each.
metric_definitions.variance: Variance of the count over the cell's windows, with one degree of freedom removed; the hurdle's is (1 - pi) (v + m^2) - ((1 - pi) m)^2 for the zero-truncated Poisson's mean m and variance v.
metric_definitions.variance_mean_slope: Least-squares slope of log active variance on log active mean across one household's cells with enough active windows: about 1 for Poisson-like counts, approaching 2 when the excess variance grows with the square of the mean.

notes: Every setting and the rule that reads the result were declared in the protocol before any household was examined.
Diagnostic only: no model is changed and no inference is run.
Households are the unit across households: each household's value is the mean of its cells' log ratios, and summaries resample households.
The own reference is fitted to each cell, so its silence and means are exact by construction and are not judged.
